## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking Slack slash commands would receive a generic failure response when the Slack account tokens were configured through SecretRefs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack slash handling now keeps the monitor's matching source-config identity when selecting refreshed runtime config. That preserves resolved secret values, rejects unrelated snapshots, and still adopts compatible routing/session refreshes between invocations.

An explicitly configured slash command now takes precedence over native Slack command mode. The two modes remain mutually exclusive, so enabling a tenant command such as `/claw` does not register an additional native-command surface.

## User Impact

Slack slash commands can reply normally when bot and app tokens are supplied through SecretRefs, instead of failing after the command reaches the gateway.

## Evidence

- Added regression coverage for an unrelated runtime snapshot containing unresolved Slack token SecretRefs while the monitor holds resolved tokens.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A resumed session's managed git worktree could be deleted out from under an active agent run. Idle GC, a separate remover, or a manual `worktrees.gc` would remove the session's isolated checkout while the run was still using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. The silent counterpart also existed: a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran as if its cwd were an ordinary directory, with no checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a rewrite of the earlier approach after maintainer review. The earlier head used a process-local FIFO lease, which was an exclusive full-run mutex (a parent and a child run sharing one worktree could deadlock), leased only `cwd`, and leaned on `git worktree lock` as the admission/removal mutex even though that lock is not an atomic cross-process check-and-act.

Runs now take a shared run-lease and removal takes an exclusive claim, both stored as rows in the existing shared-state `state_leases` table. Admission and removal each run inside one `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`, which uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`src/infra/sqlite-transaction.ts`), so the read-check-write is serialized across processes by SQLite itself. That single transaction is the atomic admission/removal gate, replacing the git-lock TOCTOU. The git worktree lock is kept only as a secondary raw-Git guard, refcounted per process so a parent and a same-process child do not unlock each other.

Ownership and lifetime details:
- The lease is acquired in `prepareAgentCommandExecution` before `ensureAgentWorkspace`, so the checkout is protected during workspace-dependent preparation, not just the run body; it is released on any prepare failure and in the run's outer cleanup.
- The worktree id is resolved from the session's stored `worktree.id` binding, or by containment over the run cwd and workspace dir. A session whose authoritative binding is removed or missing fails closed rather than continuing unmanaged.
- Run leases and the removal claim are both token-owned: a run releases only its own token, and the removal claim rejects a competing live remover and clears or finalizes only under its own token, so two removers can never enter destructive work on one worktree at once.
- Dead or reused-pid owners, including a removal claim whose remover process died before finalizing, are pruned inside the same transaction via `isLockOwnerDefinitelyStale`, so a killed holder never strands the worktree.
- Lease cleanup is process-lifecycle-owned: release retries the row deletion within the call and drops the git guard only after the row is gone; a persistent state-database or git-unlock failure retains the row and guard and is retried on the next lease acquisition and at process exit, so the worktree stays protected and a stuck cleanup recovers without waiting for the process to end.
- The in-process git-lock refcount reserves its slot synchronously before awaiting the git lock, so two overlapping same-process acquisitions cannot both record one holder and let the first release drop the guard while the other run is still live.

Choosing the shared state DB over sidecar claim files follows the repository storage policy (SQLite only for runtime registries), and reuses the cross-process lease table and transaction primitive already used by startup-migration checkpoints.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC, a manual gc, or session cleanup, including during workspace preparation, when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree, and when a second process races the removal. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files. Concurrent parent and child runs share one worktree without deadlocking, and two removers cannot corrupt a worktree by deleting it concurrently.

## Evidence

- Branched off `origin/main`; head `c4717de4`. Mergeable, behind current main.
- Focused suites pass. `src/commands/agent.worktree-race.test.ts` drives the real `prepareAgentCommandExecution` to prove the workspace-preparation window is leased and an authoritative removed binding fails closed before workspace setup. `src/agents/worktrees/run-lease.test.ts` and `src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts` cover parent/child shared readers with git-lock refcounting, workspace-only id resolution, fail-closed removed binding, dead-owner (SIGKILL) pruning, reused-pid (ABA) pruning, force parity, admission-fails-once-removing, dead-remover recovery, exclusive rejection of a second live remover (with and without force), owner-scoped abort that cannot clear a newer claim, a concurrent second remover rejected at the service level, a transient release failure recovering within one call, a sustained release failure retaining the lease and git guard and recovering on a later lifecycle retry, overlapping same-process acquisitions keeping the guard until the last release, and a git-unlock failure retained and released on a lifecycle retry. `agent.test.ts`, `agent.session.test.ts`, and the gateway worktrees/session-create/session-delete-lifecycle/server-maintenance suites pass unchanged.
- `oxlint --type-aware` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files; `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean.
- Review findings addressed across iterations: a stranded removal marker after a mid-removal crash (self-healing pid/start-time owner); an overwritable removal claim with non-owner-scoped cleanup (opaque token, exclusive rejection, owner-scoped abort); a lease acquired after workspace preparation and a removed authoritative binding that failed open (lease moved before `ensureAgentWorkspace`, fail-closed binding); a non-retryable cleanup that dropped the git guard on a failed delete (bounded retry within the single release, guard retained until success); and cleanup ownership plus a concurrent refcount race (process-lifecycle-owned retry of a stuck row-delete or git-unlock, and a synchronous refcount reservation before the git lock await).

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: the managed worktree must stay protected while the production run preparation reads or creates files and a separate process races removal; a session whose bound worktree was removed must fail admission before workspace setup instead of running without its checkout; and two removers must not enter destructive removal of one worktree at once.
Real environment tested: the real `prepareAgentCommandExecution` preparation path plus the real `ManagedWorktreeService` and the real shared-state SQLite lease store, driven on pristine `origin/main` `f73c5541` versus this patch `c4717de4` with identical inputs. The production path is driven with only config and plugin-registry loaders mocked (the real worktree service, registry, session store, and workspace step stay real, with the workspace step paused to hold the preparation window open). A second capture drives a genuine two-process race: a separate node process holds the run lease while the parent issues the removal, and a second overlapping removal is issued against the real service.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: run the composed preparation test with observations recorded (`OPENCLAW_PROOF_OUT=... run-vitest src/commands/agent.worktree-race.test.ts`), and run the two-process harness (`node --import tsx proof-lease.mts`) that creates a real session-owned git worktree with a nested workspace file, spawns a separate node process that acquires the run lease, issues non-force `ManagedWorktreeService` removals from the parent during and after the run, and issues a second overlapping removal.
Evidence after fix:
```
### production run preparation
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main f73c5541)
removal during production workspace preparation: removed=true
managed checkout survived preparation: false
admission for a removed authoritative binding: preparation proceeded without its checkout
workspace setup ran on the removed worktree: true
# AFTER (this patch c4717de4, identical inputs)
removal during production workspace preparation: rejected: worktree is busy: locked by live pid 3081575
managed checkout survived preparation: true
admission for a removed authoritative binding: preparation fails: managed worktree was removed: .../worktrees/0cdd07f48a6b9ed0/race-session
workspace setup ran on the removed worktree: false

### two-process race against the real service
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main f73c5541)
separate-process run holder: run holds no lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: removed=true
nested in-flight file survived the removal attempt: false
removal after the run ends: rejected: unknown active worktree: 3df12926-0ce3-4056-8e1f-7dd110679a02
second remover racing the first: rejected: git worktree remove failed: fatal: '.../proof-concurrent' is not a working tree
# AFTER (this patch c4717de4, identical inputs)
separate-process run holder: run holds a lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: rejected: worktree is busy: locked by live pid 3081778
nested in-flight file survived the removal attempt: true
removal after the run ends: removed=true
second remover racing the first: rejected: worktree removal is already in progress
```
Observed result after fix: during production run preparation a racing removal is rejected as busy and the checkout survives, and a session bound to a removed worktree fails preparation before workspace setup runs; in the two-process race a separate process holding the run lease has its checkout preserved while a non-force removal is rejected and only succeeds after the run ends, and a second remover racing the first is rejected as already in progress. On the base, the same removals delete the live checkout and its in-flight file, preparation proceeds without a checkout and runs workspace setup on the removed worktree, and two removers collide into a corrupt half-removed worktree.
What was not tested: no live provider request, gateway deployment, or multi-host run was exercised; the two racing processes ran on the development Linux host sharing one state directory and git worktree, so cross-process protection rests on the directly exercised SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialization plus the on-disk git worktree lock; the production preparation capture mocks only the config and plugin-registry loaders and drives the real preparation, worktree service, registry, and session store.

target.title: fix(agents): surface utility-model narration failures and show the utility model in models status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Utility-model narration (#103463, #103769) fails silently when its credential is dead. Observed live on the Molty gateway: the primary model rides Codex OAuth, but the derived utility model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna`) resolves the `openai:api-key` auth profile, which held a revoked key. Every narration call 401ed, the narrator disabled itself after 2 consecutive failures, and Discord kept showing the old raw tool lines — with zero operator-visible signal:

- narrator failures were `logVerbose`-only, and the log line did not name the agent, model, or auth profile;
- `openclaw models status` never mentioned the utility model, so nothing showed that narration depends on a different auth path than the primary.

Fixes #104764.

## Why This Change Was Made

A dead utility credential silently degrades the product experience (narrated progress drafts fall back to raw tool lines). The failure needs to be visible at default log levels and the utility model needs to be inspectable in `models status`, which owns runtime auth visibility (`--probe`/`--check`).

## User Impact

- When narration disables after consecutive failures, the gateway now logs one warn per turn: `narration disabled after 2 consecutive failures (openai/gpt-5.6-luna via openai:api-key): OpenAI API error (401): …` — naming exactly what to repair.
- `openclaw models status` shows a `Utility model` line (explicit config / provider default / disabled) and a `utilityModel: { ref, source }` field in `--json`.

## Evidence

- Live root-cause log (Molty gateway, 2026-07-11 22:25Z): `progress-narrator: completion failed: OpenAI API error (401): 401 Incorrect API key provided: sk-proj-…` repeated per turn while Discord rendered old-style tool lines; details in #104764.
- Testbox (blacksmith, lease `tbx_01kx9pjsm0ct72rze4k3ks3zzh`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29171446325)): `pnpm format:check` green; `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.test.ts src/commands/models/list.status.test.ts` → 15 + 34 tests pass, including the new warn assertion and the new `utilityModel` JSON cases (explicit config and disabled).

Follow-up tracked separately in #104764: `models status --probe` routes `api_key`-profile probes through the codex app-server harness, which cannot validate an API key (needs the Codex-contract review gate).

target.title: fix(agents): keep tool_search_code stderr tail UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tool_search_code` reports child exit failures by appending the last 500 UTF-16 code units of `stderrTail` to the error message. When that 500-unit boundary falls inside an astral character (emoji or other non-BMP text), the emitted error string contains an isolated surrogate half.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository already has `sliceUtf16Safe` in `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, and an ongoing UTF-16 safe-truncation campaign has fixed the same pattern in bootstrap context (#104423), block chunks (#104441), failover details (#104487), and several other call sites. This change applies the same helper to the code-mode stderr tail path so error messages stay well-formed.

## User Impact

Error messages for failed `tool_search_code` executions that include non-BMP characters in stderr no longer contain malformed UTF-16 surrogate halves.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/agents/tool-search.stream-errors.test.ts` that emits stderr containing an emoji positioned so the raw `.slice(-500)` would produce a lone surrogate, and asserts the rejection message is well-formed.
- Local verification on current upstream `main`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-search.stream-errors.test.ts --run` -> 2 passed
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/tool-search.ts src/agents/tool-search.stream-errors.test.ts` -> exit code 0
  - `npx oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/tool-search.ts src/agents/tool-search.stream-errors.test.ts` -> all matched files use correct format

## Competition / linked PR analysis

A fresh search found no open PR changing the stderr tail truncation in `src/agents/tool-search.ts` or the target regression test.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** malformed UTF-16 in error strings can render as replacement characters or break later text handling.
- **Risk labels considered:** error-messages.
- **Risk explanation:** the tail may now end one code unit earlier when the 500-unit boundary bisects a surrogate pair. The error message remains human-readable and the total length stays bounded.

## What Problem This Solves

#104518: an `--on-exit` cron job created with `--delete-after-run` runs its payload successfully but is retained as a **disabled** job instead of being deleted — the reporter needed a manual `cron rm`. Root cause is a two-part interaction, exactly as the triage identified: the gateway exit watcher durably disables an on-exit job **before** firing it (`persistCompletion` → `enabled: false`, the fail-closed replay protection so a gateway restart cannot re-arm and re-run the watched command), and the successful delete-after-run finalization in `applyJobResult` was restricted to `schedule.kind === "at"` — so no transition ever removed the fired job.

## Why This Change Was Made

Per the triage's best solution ("generalize successful delete-after-run finalization to supported one-shot schedules … preserving durable pre-fire replay protection"):

- `shouldDelete` in `src/cron/service/timer.ts` now covers every one-shot schedule kind (`"at"` and `"on-exit"`), still gated on `deleteAfterRun === true && status === "ok"`.
- The pre-fire disable ordering is untouched — replay protection stays durable and fail-closed; deletion is the service-owned terminal transition after a successful run, flowing through the same `applyJobResult` consumer used by both the timer path and the force path the exit watcher actually fires (`cron.run(jobId, "force")` → `ops.ts` delete branch).
- Failed runs keep the existing contract: retained (disabled) for inspection, deletion only on `ok` — same as `at` jobs.

## User Impact

`openclaw cron add --on-exit ... --delete-after-run` now behaves like the documented one-shot cleanup for `--at` jobs: success removes the job; no more zombie disabled entries needing manual `cron rm`.

## Evidence

**Regression** (`ops.regression.test.ts`, drives the same disabled-job force path the exit watcher fires, per the triage's coverage list):
- successful `deleteAfterRun` on-exit job → **removed from the store**;
- `deleteAfterRun: false` → retained, durably disabled with `lastStatus: "ok"` (persistence-order contract unchanged);
- failed run with `deleteAfterRun: true` → retained disabled with the error state preserved.

**Fails on prior head for the reported reason:** `expected { id: 'onexit-delete-ok', …(11) } to be undefined` — the job was retained disabled, byte-for-byte the reported behavior.

**Validation:** `ops.regression.test.ts` 12/12; `timer.regression.test.ts` 72/72 (includes the existing `at`-schedule deleteAfterRun retry/delete coverage, unchanged); `tsgo:core` 0; oxlint/oxfmt clean. Prod diff is the one guarded condition plus its ownership comment.

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts

```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(channels): fix five channel lifecycle/shutdown bugs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Five small channel reliability bugs where lifecycle/shutdown paths can leak timers, unhandled rejections, or ignore abort signals.

1. **iMessage RPC client** `stop()` left a 500ms SIGTERM fallback timer running when the child process had already exited, keeping the event loop alive unnecessarily.
2. **Telegram webhook** shutdown could produce an unhandled promise rejection if `bot.stop()` or transport close threw inside the abort listener.
3. **Telegram ingress worker** `stop()` was not idempotent and could leak a second 15s terminate timer; `worker.terminate()` rejections were unhandled.
4. **Telegram probe** transport cache eviction closed the oldest transport with `void transport.close()`, so a rejecting `close()` became an unhandled rejection.
5. **ClickClack gateway** reconnect backoff used a raw `setTimeout` that ignored `abortSignal`, so stopping the gateway could wait the full reconnect delay. It also leaked an abort listener on every normal reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made
- iMessage: store the fallback timer, `unref` it, and clear it once the child-close race settles.
- Telegram webhook: catch shutdown errors inside the abort paths, route them to `runtime.error`, and continue owned transport/status cleanup even if `bot.stop()` rejects.
- Telegram ingress worker: guard `stop()` with a `stopped` flag and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.
- Telegram probe: wrap the close result with `Promise.resolve(...).catch(...)` so both sync and async rejections are swallowed safely.
- ClickClack gateway: reconnect backoff uses the shared `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, treating abort rejection as normal gateway termination instead of a local timer/listener.
- Telegram probe test: use `vi.stubEnv` for `NODE_ENV`/`VITEST` so Vitest teardown restores them, instead of direct `process.env` assignment that leaked production-mode values to worker siblings.

This update also fixes the `check-test-types` failures reported by ClawSweeper (iMessage child mock typing and ClickClack config narrowing) and strengthens the iMessage test to assert the timer is cleared immediately on settlement, not only after it would have fired.

## User Impact
Cleaner shutdown for channel gateways and fewer uncaught/unhandled rejection crashes during abort, restart, or transport eviction.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2.

The proof now includes a standalone real-gateway run for the ClickClack reconnect backoff fix (local HTTP + WebSocket servers driving the real `startClickClackGatewayAccount` production function), plus the regression-test negative controls used earlier.

### ClickClack gateway: real reconnect run with local servers

This script starts real local HTTP and WebSocket servers, configures `startClickClackGatewayAccount` to point at them, waits for the websocket cycle to start, forces a reconnect, then aborts. With the fix the gateway run resolves in ~50 ms instead of waiting the configured 60 s reconnect delay.

```bash
node --import tsx proof-clickclack-reconnect.mts
```

```typescript
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import type { ChannelGatewayContext } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-contract";
import { startClickClackGatewayAccount } from "./extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.js";
import type { ResolvedClickClackAccount } from "./extensions/clickclack/src/types.js";

function assert(description: string, condition: boolean) {
  if (condition) console.log(`  ok: ${description}`);
  else { console.log(`  FAIL: ${description}`); process.exitCode = 1; }
}

async function startClickClackMockServers() {
  const connections: WebSocket[] = [];
  const httpServer = createServer((req, res) => {
    const url = new URL(req.url ?? "/", `http://localhost`);
    res.setHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");
    if (url.pathname === "/api/me") {
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ user: { id: "bot-1", display_name: "Bot", handle: "bot", avatar_url: "", created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }));
    } else if (url.pathname === "/api/realtime/events") {
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ events: [] }));
    } else {
      res.statusCode = 404;
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: "not found" }));
    }
  });
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ server: httpServer });
  wss.on("connection", (ws) => { connections.push(ws); });
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => httpServer.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const addr = httpServer.address() as AddressInfo;
  return { httpUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${addr.port}`, httpServer, wss, connections };
}

async function main() {
  const { httpUrl, httpServer, wss, connections } = await startClickClackMockServers();
  const abort = new AbortController();
  const ctx: ChannelGatewayContext<ResolvedClickClackAccount> = {
    cfg: { channels: { clickclack: { baseUrl: httpUrl, token: "test-token", workspace: "wsp_test", reconnectMs: 60_000 } } } as any,
    accountId: "default",
    account: {} as ResolvedClickClackAccount,
    runtime: {} as any,
    abortSignal: abort.signal,
    log: { warn: () => {}, info: () => {}, error: () => {}, debug: () => {} },
    getStatus: () => ({ accountId: "default" }) as any,
    setStatus: () => {},
  };

  const start = Date.now();
  const runPromise = startClickClackGatewayAccount(ctx);

  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    const check = setInterval(() => { if (connections.length > 0) { clearInterval(check); resolve(); } }, 10);
  });

  for (const ws of connections) ws.close();
  abort.abort();
  await runPromise;
  const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

  assert(`gateway run resolved in under 5s (actual ${elapsed}ms)`, elapsed < 5_000);

  httpServer.close();
  wss.close();
  console.log("\nPROOF ASSERTIONS: all passed");
}

main().catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });
```

Terminal output (fix):

```text
=== ClickClack reconnect backoff real behavior proof ===
Node: v22.22.0

[case 1] startClickClackGatewayAccount aborts promptly during reconnect backoff
  ok: gateway run resolved in under 5s (actual 50ms)
  ok: reconnectMs was 60s, so a raw setTimeout would have hung

[case 2] raw setTimeout reconnect wait ignores abort (negative control)
  ok: raw setTimeout wait did NOT resolve early (actual 5002ms >= 4500ms)
  ok: resolved flag is false because the 60s timer never fired

=== Summary ===
PROOF ASSERTIONS: all passed
```

The second case demonstrates the old raw-`setTimeout` behavior: aborting has no effect, so the wait continues for the full delay. The first case shows the fixed production gateway reacting to abort immediately while a real reconnect delay is pending.

### Regression-test negative controls

These temporarily restore the `origin/main` source for each fix, run the relevant test to reproduce the bug, then restore the fix and show the test passes.

#### ClickClack reconnect backoff ignores abort

Negative control (`extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
$ timeout 12 pnpm test extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts -- --run -t "exits immediately when aborted during reconnect backoff"
[test] test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts exited by signal SIGTERM
exit=124 (timeout/hang)
```

Fix restored:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts -- --run -t "exits immediately when aborted during reconnect backoff"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 6 skipped (7)
   Duration  4.57s
exit=0
```

#### iMessage SIGTERM fallback timer leak

Negative control (`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts` from `origin/main`):

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts -- --run -t "clears the SIGTERM fallback timer"
 FAIL  |extension-imessage| extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts > IMessageRpcClient.stop > clears the SIGTERM fallback timer
AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0
    expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBe(0)
exit=1
```

Fix restored:

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/client.test.ts -- --run -t "clears the SIGTERM fallback timer"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
   Duration  912ms
exit=0
```

#### Telegram webhook unhandled rejection on shutdown

target.title: fix(workboard): resolve parent dependency status via targeted lookups, not a full-corpus scan
target.body:
### Problem

`WorkboardStore.dependencyTargetStatus()` (`extensions/workboard/src/store.ts`)
checks whether a card's parent(s) are `done` before promoting it out of a
dependency-held status. To do that, it called the fully **unscoped**
`this.list()` — every card, on every board, fully materialized via
`entries()` + `readCard()` — and built a `Map` from it, just to look up 1-2
parent ids.

`dispatch()` calls `promoteDependencyReady()` (which calls
`dependencyTargetStatus()`) once per card in its board-scoped dispatch pass.
So every parented card being checked in a single dispatch pass re-paid for a
full-corpus re-scan: **O(parented_cards_in_pass × total_corpus_size ×
queries_per_card)**. `readCard()` alone issues 4 separate synchronous SQL
statements per row (metadata, events, child rows, labels), so on a
multi-thousand-row corpus this is thousands of synchronous SQL round-trips
per dispatch pass, once per parented card.

### How this was found

Root-caused via a live CDP CPU profile of a real, reproducible
`openclaw workboard dispatch --board <board>` call that was taking 160s+
wall-clock on a corpus of ~5770 cards, despite the dispatch handler's own
instrumented pass timers reporting well under 1 second. Attached Node's
inspector (`--inspect`) to the already-running gateway process, used
`Profiler.start`/`Profiler.stop` over the CDP protocol scoped exactly around
a real reproduction of the stall (161.8s elapsed, matching the known
symptom), and analyzed the resulting `.cpuprofile`.

**93.3% of the profiled wall-clock time** (142s self-time in a native `all()`
binding + 8.7s in `prepare()`, out of 162s total) was attributed to one call
chain:

```
dispatch()
  -> promoteDependencyReady()
    -> dependencyTargetStatus()
      -> list()
        -> entries()
          -> readCard()  (4 sync SQL statements per row)
```

This ruled out the leading working theory for this class of symptom (generic
Node event-loop starvation from a concurrent embedded/CLI agent session
monopolizing the process, as tracked in #84903 / #101895) — for this
specific, reproducible stall, the entire cost is inside the dispatch call's
own synchronous execution, not contention with unrelated work. The call
stack's `runMicrotasks → processTicksAndRejections → (root)` frames above the
hot path are simply how V8's CPU profiler represents async/await
continuations between awaited promises; they are not evidence of a different
concurrent job running.

### Fix

Replace the unscoped `list()` + `Map` lookup with targeted `get(parentId)`
calls — `get()` is already a single indexed-row lookup
(`this.store.lookup(id)`) used everywhere else in this file:

```ts
// before
const cards = new Map((await this.list()).map((entry) => [entry.id, entry]));
const parentsDone = parents.every((parentId) => cards.get(parentId)?.status === "done");

// after
const parentCards = await Promise.all(parents.map((parentId) => this.get(parentId)));
const parentsDone = parentCards.every((parent) => parent?.status === "done");
```

Complexity drops from O(total corpus size) to O(`parents.length`) — normally
1, since `cardParentIds()` already dedupes. Behavior is unchanged:
`parent?.status === "done"` on the `get()` result is exactly what
`cards.get(parentId)?.status === "done"` computed from the unscoped `list()`
Map for both the found and not-found (`undefined`) cases.

### Testing

- New regression test in `store.test.ts`
  (`"resolves parent dependency status with targeted lookups instead of a
  full-corpus scan"`): creates 1 parent + 8 children with `parents: [parent.id]`,
  spies on the underlying keyed store's `entries()`, completes the parent, runs
  `dispatch()`, and asserts:
  - all 8 children are promoted to `ready` (functional correctness, unchanged
    from before the fix)
  - `entries()` is called **at most once** during the dispatch pass — before
    the fix this would have been 9 calls (1 outer board-scoped `list()` + 1
    inner unscoped `list()` per parented card being checked)
- Full extension suite: **113/113 pass**
  (`npx vitest run extensions/workboard/src/`)

### Scope note

`dependsOn()` (same file) has an identical unscoped-`list()` pattern, used
only for cycle-detection at parent/child link-creation time — not on the
dispatch hot path, and there's no profiling evidence it's ever expensive in
practice (link creation is comparatively rare). Deliberately left out of this
PR to keep the change matched 1:1 to the measured problem; worth a follow-up
if it's ever shown to be hot.

### Relationship to #101895 / #84903

#101895 was our earlier report of this exact symptom (`workboard.cards.dispatch`
taking 250s+ wall-clock), which was auto-triaged as a duplicate and merged into
#84903 (generic event-loop-starvation tracker) under the theory that a
concurrent embedded/CLI agent session was starving the gateway's single event
loop. The live CPU profile above shows that, for this specific stall, that
theory doesn't hold — the cost is entirely inside `dispatch()`'s own
synchronous execution. Leaving a comment on both issues linking back to this
PR; the general event-loop-starvation question tracked in #84903 may still be
real for other symptoms, but this particular reproduction is fully explained
and fixed by the change here.

Verified locally against a real corpus (~5770 Workboard cards): the exact
`workboard.cards.dispatch` RPC call that took 160-163s wall-clock before this
fix consistently completed in **2.9s** after, with internal pass-timer
instrumentation showing the fix itself added no measurable overhead
(<1ms, consistent with pre-fix internal timings).


### Real behavior proof

Redacted excerpt from the deployed instance's own gateway log, straight from
`journalctl`, showing repeated real `workboard.cards.dispatch` RPC calls
against a live board with a ~5,770-card corpus, immediately before and after
this fix was deployed (connection/request IDs already truncated by the
logger itself; nothing else redacted):

**Before** (unscoped `list()` scan on every parented card in the pass):
```

2026-07-11T18:47:39.256Z [ws] res workboard.cards.dispatch 154351ms

```

**After** (targeted `get(parentId)` lookups; internal `pass_total`
instrumentation, unrelated to this PR, confirms the fix itself adds no
measurable overhead — consistently under 1 second before and after):

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a parked in-flight create cannot be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name retry (same-owner and foreign-owner both covered, setup executes exactly once); a failing setup leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).
- `list()` now shows a worktree from claim-time (during provisioning) rather than after setup completes; failed creates still end with no registry row.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> atomic path claim -> re-provision

  -> claim loser (concurrent registration won): touches nothing; standard in-use semantics
  -> gc: preserve-only (unchanged upstream behavior)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- retried create succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record); gc preserves the orphan untouched.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41) agents shard + 23 passed state shard
```

Real-behavior proof on the FROZEN FINAL head e5b7677497 (all four requested scenarios — active holder survives gc, SIGKILLed holder reaped after lease expiry and recreated fully provisioned, missing-path claim cleaned to a retriable name, pre-column DB backfills ready): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4947439791. Earlier ordering-specific transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4944938951 — Window B is a genuine mid-provisioning SIGKILL (exit 137) showing the crash state is observable (claim-time row, missing setup marker), gc preserves it, and the operator recovery path works end-to-end (remove() cleans worktree+branch, fresh create fully provisions); Window A (add→claim, no user code) is a labeled constructed end-state recovered by retried-create adoption with full re-provisioning. Supersedes the earlier transcript (#issuecomment-4937129438), which demonstrated the pre-claim-early ordering.

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

The previously-acknowledged gc-vs-create double-insert race is now eliminated by the atomic path claim (deterministic interleaving tests cover both directions, with a pasted negative control showing the pre-claim code produces the duplicate row). Remaining narrow edge deliberately out of scope: a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.

target.title: fix(signal): include quoted reply context for agents
target.body:
Closes #98287
Related: #98234 (non-duplicate reply-session initialization conflict/drop issue)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal users sending quoted replies could have the quoted target extracted into `ReplyToBody` metadata while the agent-facing `BodyForAgent` remained only the new ambiguous message, such as `Did this get done?`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now renders visible quoted-reply context directly into `BodyForAgent` as a clear blockquote while preserving clean `RawBody`, `CommandBody`, and `BodyForCommands` for command parsing and hooks. The shared inbound metadata renderer skips only the duplicate one-hop reply-target block when the Signal-generated wrapper exactly matches the expected quoted body and sender; richer `ReplyChain` context and ordinary user-authored blockquotes still render normally.

## User Impact

Signal quoted replies now carry the referenced message into agent-facing input, so agents can answer ambiguous followups using the intended quoted target. Plain non-quoted Signal messages remain unchanged, and quoted context is not duplicated in the model prompt when Signal has already inlined the generated quote block.

## Evidence

Duplicate search before filing found no open narrow issue/PR for `Signal quoted reply BodyForAgent` / `agent-facing body`; the closest existing items were closed #68665 and related-but-different #84364, plus broad open quote-reply PRs that do not provide this narrow BodyForAgent fix.

Validation run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts`

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src` (29 files, 375 tests)
- `git diff --check`
- Exact-head regression coverage now canonicalizes blank lines in multi-paragraph quoted text (`>` with no trailing space) and proves the duplicate metadata block stays suppressed.
- Debounced Signal batches now render reply context per entry before joining the batch, with quoted-first/plain-last and plain-first/quoted-last regressions and an internal exact-once marker that preserves the last structured reply metadata without duplicating it in the prompt.
- Fresh GitHub CI is running after the only preceding failure—two formatter-only line wraps in the Signal handler—was fixed on exact head `8087d6f852d51bf20dd0bca1d13c900219d6e3ed`, which includes the shared upstream cutoff `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`.

Confirm no accepted duplicate-context, equal-body, spoofed marker/altered wrapper, ReplyChain, or command/raw body regressions remain.'` clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
